summary: This note describes the Robert E. Lee Monument in New Orleans, dedicated in 1884 at Tivoli Circle (commonly called Lee Circle) on St. Charles Avenue. It covers the dedication attendees, the fundraising by the Robert E. Lee Monument Association after Lee's 1870 death, and the hiring of sculptor Alexander Doyle. It also lists the contracts and costs for the base, pedestal and column.
one_line: A note on the 1884 Robert E. Lee Monument at Tivoli (Lee) Circle in New Orleans, covering its dedication, funding, sculptor and construction costs.
key_facts: The Robert E. Lee Monument was dedicated in 1884 at Tivoli Circle, since commonly called Lee Circle, on St. Charles Avenue.
The dedication took place on February 22, George Washington's birthday.
Former Confederate President Jefferson Davis was among the dignitaries present at the monument's dedication.
Two daughters of General Robert E. Lee were present at the dedication of the monument.
Confederate General P.G.T. Beauregard was present at the monument's dedication.
Fundraising for the statue began after Lee's death in 1870, led by the Robert E. Lee Monument Association.
By 1876 the Robert E. Lee Monument Association had raised the $36,400 needed to build the statue.
The association's president was Louisiana Supreme Court Justice Charles E. Fenner.
New York sculptor Alexander Doyle was hired to sculpt the statue.
John Ray (Roy), architect, designed and built the base and pedestal under a contract dated 1877.
John Hagan, a builder, was contracted to furnish and set the column.
